== Problem ==

Two different numbers are randomly selected from the set <imath>\{ - 2, -1, 0, 3, 4, 5\}</imath> and multiplied together. What is the probability that the product is <imath>0</imath>?

<imath>\textbf{(A) }\dfrac{1}{6}\qquad\textbf{(B) }\dfrac{1}{5}\qquad\textbf{(C) }\dfrac{1}{4}\qquad\textbf{(D) }\dfrac{1}{3}\qquad \textbf{(E) }\dfrac{1}{2}</imath>

== Solutions==

===Solution 1===
1. Identify the total number of ways to select two different numbers from the set:

The set has 6 elements. The number of ways to choose 2 different numbers from 6 is given by the combination formula: <imath>\binom{6}{2} = \frac{6 \times 5}{2 \times 1} = 15</imath>.

2. Identify the favorable outcomes:

For the product to be zero, one of the chosen numbers must be zero. The set contains one zero (0). To have a product of zero, we need to choose 0 and any other number from the remaining five numbers <imath>-2, -1, 3, 4, 5</imath>.

The number of ways to choose 0 and one other number from the remaining five is 5.

3. Calculate the probability:

The probability is the number of favorable outcomes divided by the total number of outcomes: <imath>\text{Probability} = \frac{\text{Number of favorable outcomes}}{\text{Total number of outcomes}} = \frac{5}{15} = \frac{1}{3}</imath>.

Thus, the probability that the product is <imath>0</imath> is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)} \ \frac{1}{3}}.</imath>

~GeometryMystery

===Solution 2 (Complementary Counting)===
Because the only way the product of the two numbers is <imath>0</imath> is if one of the numbers we choose is <imath>0,</imath> we calculate the probability of NOT choosing a <imath>0.</imath> We get <imath>\frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{4}{5} = \frac{2}{3}.</imath> Therefore our answer is <imath>1 - \frac{2}{3} = \boxed{\textbf{(D)} \ \frac{1}{3}}.</imath>

===Solution 3(One Sentence!!!)===
1/6 * Any other number + Any other number * 1/6 = 1/6+1/6 = <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)} \ \frac{1}{3}}</imath>

-JasonDaGoat


1/6 Chance of 0 * A number in the set + 1/6 chance of A number in the set * 0 = 1/6+1/6 = <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(D)} \ \frac{1}{3}}</imath>.

===Solution 4===
To get a product of <imath>0</imath>, one of the numbers must be <imath>0</imath>, which means that we have <imath>2P1=2</imath> possible combinations of a random number from the set, and <imath>0</imath>. There is <imath>6</imath> total possible products, giving us <imath>\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}</imath>.
